dovish.title: Labour Market Softening
dovish.summary: Job market is cracking: payrolls went negative, far below forecast.
dovish.reason: Payrolls turned negative and prior months were revised lower, signalling a labour-demand inflection. UPDATE 8/28: NFP benchmark revision resolved benign at -79k total nonfarm (-0.1%, private -178k) — far smaller than the -620k tail risk carried earlier, though below ~+163k analyst consensus. Warsh directly contradicted the cracking narrative at Jackson Hole: labour 'consistent with full employment', jobless 4.1%, 4-week avg claims near multi-decade lows (8/27 claims 203k vs 208k fcst). Weight trimmed 2.0 -> 1.5.

dovish.title: ISM Manufacturing Back in Contraction
dovish.summary: Factories are shrinking again — demand is cooling, not overheating.
dovish.reason: Sub-50 S&P Global flash manufacturing (48.7), soft orders and employment point to weaker demand, while lower prices paid reduce the inflation obstacle to easing. Note: ISM proper printed 55.6 last release — Sep 1 ISM mfg (fcst 55.3 per FXStreet) is the arbiter between the two surveys. Chicago PMI moved to Mon 8/31 (fcst 57.0).

dovish.title: Consumer and Industrial Chain Under Pressure
dovish.summary: Consumer engine sputtering: biggest US retailer cut guidance.
dovish.reason: Softer retail guidance and industrial orders can transmit through earnings, hiring and consumption. UPDATE 8/28: UoM final sentiment 51.7 beat 51.0 fcst — sentiment leg stabilizing; story aging, weight trimmed 1.5 -> 1.0.

dovish.title: Long-End Easing Continues — Passive Tightening Fading
dovish.summary: 10Y -0.4% w / 30Y -1.3% w still net lower, but post-Warsh bounce (+4.8bp d) challenges the trend.
dovish.reason: Weekly trend still marginally dovish (10Y 4.720% from 4.738%, 30Y 5.206% from 5.276%) but Friday's +4.8bp 10Y backup on the hawkish Warsh speech is a direct challenge. If 10Y re-takes 4.75%+ next week this driver flips hawkish. Held at 1.0 pending Monday.

dovish.title: Equity Rally Confirms Risk-On Into Jackson Hole
dovish.summary: SPY +0.5% w but Friday stalled post-Warsh; small-caps hit hardest (IWM -1.35% d).
dovish.reason: Fri 2026-08-28: post-Warsh stall — SPY -0.23%, QQQ -0.65%, IWM -1.35% on the day; weekly still green for mega-caps (SPY +0.47%, QQQ +0.42%) but IWM -1.40% w. Rate-sensitive small caps sold the hawkish speech first. Weekly resilience keeps the driver, daily reversal caps it at 1.0.

dovish.title: Oil Demand-Scare — Cumulative Hit Intact
dovish.summary: WTI -4.2% w — demand scare deepened; disinflation tailwind for the doves.
dovish.reason: WTI $83.44, now -4.16% w — the demand-scare repricing deepened through Friday. Consistent with ISM mfg flash 48.7, negative payrolls and weak China PMIs; a direct disinflation impulse that argues for cuts even as Warsh stresses sticky services inflation.

dovish.title: VIX at Multi-Week Low — Calmest Tape Pre-Jackson Hole
dovish.summary: VIX 14.43, -4.6% w — market shrugged off even a hawkish Warsh; complacency itself is dovish-friendly.
dovish.reason: VIX fell to 14.43 even as Warsh delivered a hawkish Jackson Hole speech — markets refuse to price a hawkish tail. Low vol keeps financial conditions easy, which ironically argues against cuts; but as a sentiment gauge it remains dovish-friendly. Held at 1.0.

dovish.title: UoM 1Y Inflation Expectations Drop to 4.0%
dovish.summary: Inflation expectations fell back toward the anchor — the de-anchoring scare eased.
dovish.source: University of Michigan final Aug (via FXStreet calendar)
dovish.reason: Final August 1Y expectations 4.0% vs 4.3% forecast and 4.5% 8/15 prelim — the mid-month de-anchoring spike reversed. Directly defuses the prior hawkish expectations driver (retired) and hands doves a fresh data point ahead of Sep FOMC.

hawkish.title: Services PMI Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Services economy is running hot, not slowing.
hawkish.reason: Strong services demand, employment and prices paid point to persistent core-services inflation and raise the hurdle for a cut. Warsh cited exactly this stickiness at Jackson Hole (54% of PCE basket >3% 12m). Sep 3 ISM Services (prev 54.1) is the next test.

hawkish.title: Tariff Inflation Shock
hawkish.summary: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while expectations are already elevated.
hawkish.reason: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while expectations are already elevated. First post-tariff Core PCE now expected in the Sep 5 window (not in FXStreet 7-day calendar); UoM 1Y final fell to 4.0% — softening the expectations leg, but the tariff impulse itself is untouched.

hawkish.title: Hawkish 3-Vote Dissent at July FOMC
hawkish.summary: Three regional Fed presidents wanted a hike at the last meeting — the Committee is split.
hawkish.reason: Re-verified 2026-08-28 via federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm: 9-3 hold with Hammack, Kashkari, Logan preferring +25bp. Warsh's Aug 28 speech ('predominant focus on prices', 'otherwise we have work to do') moved the Chair rhetorically toward the dissenters — the hawkish cluster is no longer isolated.

hawkish.title: Gold's Record Run — Inflation-Hedge Bid Persists
hawkish.summary: GC=F $4504 (-2.3% d, -2.6% w): post-Warsh hawkish repricing broke the inflation-hedge bid.
hawkish.reason: Gold dumped -2.29% (GC=F 4504.1, off the $4648 peak) as markets took Warsh hawkish — real-yield pressure beat the inflation-hedge bid. Driver kept at reduced 0.5 to preserve stable ID; if GC=F holds below $4500 the record-run signal is broken.

hawkish.title: Warsh Jackson Hole: 'Predominant Focus on Prices'
hawkish.summary: Fed Chair Warsh: inflation is the predominant focus — no cut pre-commitment, 'otherwise we have work to do'.
hawkish.source: Federal Reserve — Chair Warsh, 'In Our Time', Jackson Hole

data.previous: July stmt: solid growth, elevated uncertainty

hawkish.reason: Warsh: 'the Fed's predominant focus right now should be on prices'; labour 'consistent with full employment' (4.1% jobless, claims near multi-decade lows); financial conditions 'hard pressed to describe as restrictive'; 'committed to a discipline, not to a decision'. Markets read it hawkish: ZQ=F -0.16 to 96.215 (implied 3.785%, +16bp over mid), GC=F -2.29%, 10Y +4.8bp, IWM -1.35%. Sep cut odds repriced from 55% to 45% on this desk's proxy.

dovish.title: US-Canada Reciprocal Tariffs
dovish.summary: US tariffs hit Canada's export engine first and hardest.
dovish.reason: Canada's US-demand exposure means tariffs can cut export orders and output. UPDATE 8/28: Q2 GDP +0.8% QoQ LED BY EXPORTS — economy weathering tariffs far better than feared; drag narrative weakened, weight 2.0 -> 1.5. Structural exposure remains.

dovish.title: Household Leverage and Mortgage Sensitivity
dovish.summary: Highly indebted households cannot absorb today's rates.
dovish.reason: High leverage and mortgage renewals make Canadian demand unusually sensitive to elevated rates. Q2 GDP showed household spending contributing and saving rate 3.7% — structural driver, aging; weight 1.5 -> 1.0.

dovish.title: Global Manufacturing Pullback
dovish.summary: Global factory slowdown leads Canadian exports lower.
dovish.reason: Global manufacturing weakness leads Canadian resource and industrial exports by one to two months. Sep 1 Canadian Mfg PMI (prev 53.5 per FXStreet) and US ISM (fcst 55.3) are the pre-decision reads.

dovish.title: Labour Market Marginal Easing
dovish.summary: Unemployment is creeping up — labour slack is building.
dovish.reason: Higher unemployment and slower wage growth indicate more labour-market slack. Stale (Jul 30); weight 1.0 -> 0.5 pending the Sep LFS.

dovish.title: CAD Firms Slightly — Sep 2 BoC Dovish Wedge Narrows
dovish.summary: USDCAD 1.3902 — CAD weaker through 1.39 despite the GDP beat; rate-spread trade dominates.
dovish.reason: USDCAD 1.3902 on Fri (+0.19% d, +0.88% w) — CAD weakened even with a GDP beat because the post-Warsh USD bid and Fed-BoC spread dominate. Rate-spread trade remains the cleanest dovish signal into Sep 2.

dovish.title: Oil Demand-Scare — CAD Terms of Trade Eroded
dovish.summary: WTI $83.44, -4.16% w — CAD terms of trade keep eroding into the Sep 2 decision.
dovish.reason: Oil's weekly slide deepened to -4.16%, eroding Canada's terms of trade and the BoC's hawkish buffer. Partly offset by today's strong GDP; net still dovish for the Sep 2 calculus.

hawkish.title: Retail Sales Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Consumers are still spending — no collapse in sight.
hawkish.reason: Broad retail growth (+0.6% vs +0.2% fcst) showed consumption resilience — and Q2 GDP confirmed household spending strength. Gives the BoC room to hold on Sep 2.

hawkish.title: Energy Tailwind Reversed — Marked Neutral
hawkish.summary: WTI at $83.19; energy tailwind has flipped to headwind for CAD.
hawkish.reason: WTI $83.44 (-4.16% w) — energy tailwind fully flipped to headwind. Kept at 0.5/neutral to preserve stable ID.

hawkish.title: CAD GDP Beat — Sep 2 Hold Now Base Case
hawkish.summary: Q2 GDP +0.8% QoQ led by exports; June +0.3% MoM beat — the make-or-break print broke hawkish.

data.delta_label: MoM beat +0.1; ann. -0.1 vs fcst but rebound from -0.1

hawkish.reason: StatCan verified 2026-08-28: Q2 real GDP +0.8% QoQ (~3.3% annualized), Q1 revised 0.0 -> +0.1%, led by exports, household spending and business investment. The pre-decision make-or-break printed strong — Sep 2 hold is now the base case (pricing shifted to 0.35 cut / 0.60 hold). Weight raised 1.5 -> 2.0 as the decisive domestic data point.

hawkish.title: US Stickiness Spillover — Fed Path Constrains BoC
hawkish.summary: Warsh turned hawkish at Jackson Hole; USDCAD 1.39 — a BoC cut now would widen the gap into a strong USD.
hawkish.reason: A BoC cut 5 days ahead of a hawkish Fed (Warsh: 'predominant focus on prices') would widen the rate gap into a strengthening USD — USDCAD already 1.3902 (+0.88% w). The Fed path now constrains the BoC more than at any point this year. Weight 1.0 -> 1.5.
